title: Garage Conversion Decision Workbook
subtitle: Build a feasibility packet before committing your garage, storage and construction budget.
outcome: Prepare a garage-use brief, a local-question register, a displaced-function plan and conditional area, cost and timing scenarios ending in proceed, revise or pause.
intro: For U.S. homeowners considering conversion of an existing garage, before they purchase construction. Bring accessible property documents and actual professional information; do not investigate concealed conditions to complete the sheets.

Start with the intended use and local classification questions. Then record the garage-specific assessment, displaced functions and area definition. Use the cases as examples of reasoning, not instructions to approve your site.

All amounts and weeks are invented teaching inputs. The £9.99 GBP purchase is a planning workbook, not a permit, design, valuation, insurance determination or professional review. Useful outcomes have not been tested with homeowners.

No structural, electrical, hazardous-material, moisture-remediation or other execution procedures are provided. Qualified local parties determine requirements and suitability. A completed packet may correctly end with a pause.

sections.title: Choose the use before asking for a conversion price
paras: Write the exact use you want from the garage: a room serving the existing household, sleeping accommodation, work space, or a proposed independent dwelling. Record whether cooking, bathing, separate access or separate occupancy is intended. Ask the local authority and designer how the actual proposal is classified; a marketing label such as bonus room does not settle that question.

Describe who will use the space, when and how they reach it. A room for daytime activities may not meet the same need as sleeping space or independent accommodation. Keep an alternative of retaining the garage and changing another room in the house on the decision sheet. These alternatives need not offer identical privacy, access or storage.

The workbook's result is a pre-purchase feasibility packet: a use brief, unanswered authority questions, displaced-use arrangements, defined area and conditional cost/timing scenarios. It does not provide plans, approve occupancy, establish rental rights or determine a return on investment. You can finish the packet with a decision to pause.

sections.title: Assemble the property evidence, not a presumed approval
paras: Collect accessible existing drawings, relevant permit history, previous reports and property information requested by your actual reviewer. Identify attached versus detached configuration and shared boundaries as facts to verify. A listing description or tax-area figure should remain a separate source, not proof that a garage already qualifies as living space.

Portland's conversion page distinguishes habitable-space conversion from its ADU process and discusses permit history [Portland]. It is a local example of why classification comes first. Its particular standards, parking provisions and application rules do not apply nationwide. Request the applicable process from the authority serving your property.

Give each unanswered question an owner and an evidence source: authority response, designer report, property document or provider proposal. Record preliminary advice separately from a formal decision. If cooking facilities or occupancy change during planning, ask whether the earlier advice still describes the revised project before carrying the old budget forward.

sections.title: Case 1: keep garage footprint and proposed room area distinct
paras: Invented measured planning rectangle: 22 x 20 feet gives 440 square feet of gross garage footprint. The concept reserves 40 square feet for an entry/service zone and 60 for retained storage, with non-overlapping areas. The remaining proposed room area is 440 - 40 - 60 = 340 square feet. This is an owner scope illustration, not measured legal living area.

A hypothetical $44,880 package divided by the gross footprint gives $102 per gross square foot. Dividing the same package by the proposed 340-square-foot room gives $132 per proposed-room square foot. The package did not become more expensive; the denominator changed. Neither ratio is a market benchmark or a promise that every foot can be occupied.

Ask the designer and bidder to state which area definition each quote uses and which zones receive work. Wall build-ups, retained equipment and final layout can alter the usable result. Do not treat the rectangle as proof of acceptable height, access, daylight, emergency escape, structural suitability or approval.

sections.title: Decide where the garage functions go
paras: List actual items and activities displaced by conversion: vehicle parking, bikes, tools, laundry access, household storage or hobby use. Keep decisions about disposing of items separate from an assumption that they disappear at no cost. For each retained function, name a lawful, practical replacement location and the person who must confirm it.

Check accessibility and permission for the replacement arrangement. A driveway, side yard, rented unit or another household room may have different constraints. The appropriate local parties must establish any parking or site requirements. This book gives no national parking replacement rule and does not recommend placing storage in a required route.

Estimate transport, preparation and recurring costs only from actual offers or explicitly invented scenarios. Record how long the arrangement is assumed to last. The value of keeping equipment close at hand or avoiding another daily task belongs in your non-price comparison, without inventing a cash value for convenience.

sections.title: Case 2: compare two storage replacement arrangements
paras: Invented two-year comparison for the same defined set of household items: Option A uses $650 of approved home-storage preparation, a $350 move and a rented overflow space at $95 per month for 24 months. Its stated scenario is $650 + $350 + (24 x $95) = $3,280. No new building or electrical work is implied by the preparation line.

Option B uses a different rented storage offer at $185 per month for 24 months plus the same $350 move. Its scenario is $4,790, or $1,510 more than A over that period. Assume these prices include all charges for this arithmetic exercise only. Actual contracts may include deposits, insurance, access restrictions, price changes or return moves.

The lower modeled cost does not establish that A holds the same items securely or offers suitable access. Ask for actual capacity and terms, document the expected duration and compare the functions you retain. If the conversion changes your parking arrangement as well, price and assess that separately; do not hide it inside the storage result.

sections.title: Request a garage-specific condition review
paras: Ask qualified providers to identify what they must assess about the existing structure, floor, enclosure, moisture, services and proposed use. Keep the large vehicle-door opening and the boundary to the existing house visible in the brief. The assessment must address the actual garage; a neighbor's completed conversion does not establish suitability.

Record accessible observations such as past water entry with dates, without opening assemblies, sampling materials or diagnosing the cause. EPA emphasizes controlling moisture in its mold guide [EPA moisture]. Ask the relevant professional to establish what findings must be resolved before finishes or enclosure, rather than treating paint or flooring as evidence of readiness.

For relevant older housing, EPA's consumer renovation guidance addresses lead-safe work in pre-1978 homes [EPA lead]. Ask qualified parties which requirements apply to this project. This book supplies no hazardous-material disturbance, cleanup, testing, structural, fire-separation or building-services procedure.

sections.title: Make the concept's interfaces explicit
paras: Ask the design team to explain how the proposed room connects to the occupied home or operates separately. Record the intended access, retained garage functions and the work at the former vehicle opening. These are questions for qualified design, not instructions for modifying the opening, floor or envelope.

Keep heating, cooling, ventilation, water and electrical needs tied to the exact proposed use. Ask who establishes capacity, routing, supporting work and applicable approvals. A decorative room package might not include all of those services. If a kitchen or bathroom is added later, reopen the classification and scope record.

Request alternative concepts only with their limitations stated. Retaining more storage, reducing the finished zone or choosing a different use can change both cost and usefulness. A conditional option should remain conditional until assessed. Do not rank a technically unresolved option as the cheapest viable conversion.

sections.title: Case 3: build a conditional decision envelope
paras: Invented budget lines, all non-overlapping: $1,400 initial professional assessment; $3,600 later design; $1,800 application/permit allowance; $42,000 defined conversion construction; and the $3,280 storage scenario from Case 2. Total owner scenario = $52,080. Against a $55,000 ceiling, the initial headroom is $2,920.

A later qualified finding adds $3,500 of specifically identified work not in any existing line. The revised scenario becomes $55,580, exceeding the ceiling by $580. This addition is not a percentage contingency and not a replacement of an included allowance. If a finding is already covered in the contract, do not add it twice.

The response is a decision: obtain a revised defined option, change funding with appropriate advice, or pause. Do not close the gap by deleting a required assessed item without a qualified alternative. The amounts are not current installation prices; the initial headroom never proved that the project was feasible or fully funded.

sections.title: Case 4: check dependency timing rather than adding every duration
paras: Invented simplified planning network: retrieving records takes two weeks and the professional assessment takes three weeks, both starting together. Concept work starts only when both finish, and takes two more weeks. Assume a four-week authority stage after that, then six weeks of construction. Earliest modeled finish is max(2,3) + 2 + 4 + 6 = 15 weeks.

If the authority stage instead takes seven weeks, the same model becomes 18 weeks. Adding the original parallel tasks as though they were sequential would incorrectly give 17 weeks for the first scenario. The two-week records task is still necessary, but its overlap matters. The example contains no actual authority service standard.

Ask the real team which activities can overlap and which require a confirmed predecessor. Include relevant equipment, access, review and inspection dependencies in the actual schedule; this illustration omits them. A forecast date is not approval to occupy, and a household should not make a non-refundable moving commitment from these invented weeks.

sections.title: Separate exploration spending from construction commitment
paras: Create a written decision gate before each new commitment. The first gate may authorize a defined assessment only; a later gate may authorize design or an application. Record cancellation terms and deliverables from the actual provider agreement. A planning allowance is not permission for a contractor to proceed.

Track amounts already paid, amounts contractually committed and amounts merely forecast in different columns. Do not describe fees already spent as future headroom. If the concept changes, ask which earlier records can still be used and which services need repeating; there is no universal refund or reuse promise.

Keep projected rental income, sale value and square-footage recognition outside the funding case unless supported and appropriately advised. This workbook supplies no appraisal, tax, insurance or legal conclusion. Ask relevant advisers about actual policy and property effects rather than assuming conversion automatically creates recognized living area or an income stream.

sections.title: Use the two completed records to build your packet
paras: The completed area record shows how one gross garage rectangle can produce two cost ratios without either becoming a legal-area statement. The completed decision envelope carries an initial budget through a new finding and a pause request. Both demonstrations use fictional inputs and the same prompts as their blank worksheets.

Begin with the use brief and property questions, then attach provider findings before ranking construction offers. Keep original documents and quote revisions intact. On each sheet, distinguish what the owner wants, what a professional has assessed and what the authority has actually decided. An unknown can remain an honest finished entry.

The seven sheets are summaries for communication, not substitutes for drawings or detailed schedules. Add dated attachments and remove unrelated personal details before sharing a completed copy with your providers. Your PDF entries remain in your file; the fields do not calculate or submit an application.

sections.title: Choose proceed, revise or pause with a named reason
paras: At the end of the packet, identify the unresolved condition most likely to change your decision: use classification, a garage-specific finding, an unaffordable interface, an impractical replacement function or a timing dependency. State which party must answer it and what document would close the question.

If you proceed, request a current coordinated scope and the relevant approval and completion evidence from the responsible team. If you revise, record the new use or area and update dependent costs. If you pause, retain what was learned and do not assume the same reports or rules will remain current indefinitely.

The addition and basement books cover broader space alternatives, general area records and existing-building condition questions. This workbook's distinct focus is the garage's lost functions, use-classification gate, former vehicle-opening interfaces and staged conversion decision packet. General planning methods are related; the text, cases and record sets here are newly authored.

questions: How is my exact proposed use classified locally, including any independent occupancy?
Which property and permit-history records do you need before reviewing this concept?
What garage-specific structural, floor, enclosure and service assessments are needed?
Which finding must be resolved before closing assemblies or purchasing finishes?
What happens at the former vehicle opening and the existing-house connection?
Which zones remain storage or service space, and what area does your price cover?
What parking, access or other local constraints apply to displaced garage functions?
Which design, application and supporting-work costs are outside the construction total?
Which amounts are paid, committed, provisional or only forecast?
What changes if the use, cooking facilities or proposed occupancy changes?
Which schedule activities depend on authority responses or other providers?
Which documents establish relevant approval, completion and permission for intended use?
sources: Local example: conversion permits, use/ADU distinction and permit history. No Portland code dimension or parking rule is presented as national guidance.
Moisture-control context only; no diagnosis, cleanup instructions or readiness threshold supplied.
Consumer lead-safe renovation context for relevant pre-1978 housing. Actual applicability and work belong with qualified parties.
source_limits: Primary pages retrieved October 30, 2026. Portland is one jurisdiction, not nationwide permission. EPA context supports professional questions rather than execution procedures. No organization endorses the book. All numerical cases, completed records and prompts are original hypothetical teaching material; no current market cost, rental yield, resale result or incentive is claimed.
overlap: Addition and basement books share broad space, condition and budget methods. This title adds the garage-use classification packet, displaced parking/storage, former vehicle-opening questions and staged proceed/revise/pause records. No substantive paragraph or worked case is copied. The document layout and tested delivery code are reused.
final_checks: Is the intended use specific enough for the actual authority and designer to classify it?
Are property records, owner observations, professional findings and issued approvals distinguishable?
Can you identify where every displaced garage function goes and who confirms permission and practicality?
Does every area ratio name its denominator without claiming legal living area?
Are assessment, design, supporting work and displacement costs included without double counting?
Do new findings reopen both the budget and the decision gate before commitments?
Keep a blank master and save/reopen your completed copy. Free checklist: https://homecostengine.com/blog/questions-before-budgeting-garage-conversion
